title: A Reading Nook in 2 m²: Plan It in One Afternoon
description: You don't need a library or a spare room. A corner by a window, the right lamp and one chair will do. A practical guide to a reading nook in a small flat, budget included.
excerpt: The corner that currently holds the drying rack could be the best spot in your home by Sunday. You need three things and to know where to put them.
content:
Almost every flat has one dead corner. Next to the window, between the wardrobe and the wall, at the end of the hallway. That's where a reading nook belongs — and unlike a kitchen remodel, you can pull it off in an afternoon for under $200.

## The three things it can't work without

A seat, light and a surface. Nothing else. Choose the chair by seat depth (55–60 cm is ideal) so you can actually sink into it. Solve the light with a floor lamp in warm white (2700 K) and a shade that points down at the page, not at your eyes. The surface can be a block of wood or a tiny side table — it only has to hold a mug and a book.

## Where to put it

By the window, but sideways, not facing it. Daylight then falls over your shoulder onto the page instead of putting you in backlight. No window? Pick the corner nobody walks through — a spot where you can "hide" reads completely differently from one in the middle of traffic. A rug under the chair visually separates the nook from the rest of the room and softens the sound too.

## How to see it before you buy

The classic mistake is buying the chair and then discovering it faces the wall and the lamp has no place to go. Before you order anything, photograph the corner on your phone and upload it to [RoomFlip](https://roomflip.io) — the AI shows you in seconds what the nook looks like with a specific chair, rug and lighting. Try three versions, pick one, then spend the money.

And if the plan reveals room for a couple of dumbbells too, have a look at [GymHome](https://gymhome.cz) — sometimes it's better to train elsewhere and keep home quiet for reading.
